text.arabic_uthmani: فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُۥ نَفْسُهُۥ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

words.gloss_range: immediate connective opening that binds the prior warning to the new narrated response
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) opens 5:30 as fallout from the prior warning (5:29) rather than a fresh scene. Its clipped connective force begins the ayah's three-link chain: response, killing, and loss.

topics.headline: opening fa binds prior warning to fallout
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as fallout from the previous warning rather than as a fresh independent scene.
topics.reason: The opening particle is licensed as immediate sequence and the CRITICAL rows coherently connect it to the prior speech boundary.

topics.headline: first pulse in the three-fa causal chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first small connector as the opening beat of a chain that moves from inner compliance to killing to loss.
topics.reason: The three clauses are linked by fa-particles in the attachment evidence, so the structural and cadence claims survive locally.

words.gloss_range: Form II perfect feminine verb: the possessed self caused the killing to become compliant or approachable for him
words.root_gloss_range: obedience, compliance, willingness, pliancy, and making something manageable; locally Form II causative/intensive self-prompting toward murder
words.prose: {{ar:طَوَّعَتْ}} ({{tr:ṭawwaʿat}}) makes the inner compliance grammatically complete before the killing occurs. Form II and the feminine agreement make {{ar:نَفْسُهُۥ}} ({{tr:nafsuhū}}) the agent that renders {{ar:قَتْلَ}} ({{tr:qatla}}) approachable for him, so willingness and responsibility are manufactured inside the actor rather than imposed from outside. Variant pressure may expose reciprocity or intensification, but the local surface keeps causative compliance as the governing force. The 3:168 echo reverses similar ingredients: obedience, brothers, selves, and killing become, in 5:30, internal compliance producing fratricide.

topics.headline: perfect verb completes the inner compliance before the act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the psychology is presented as already accomplished before the killing is narrated.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect verb and the clause order places this completed internal process before the killing beat.

topics.headline: feminine agreement makes the self the agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the person split into a self that acts, a possessor for whom it acts, and an act made approachable.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the self the subject, the killing the object, and the lām phrase the affected recipient.

topics.headline: obedience and willingness become morally inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that vocabulary associated with willing compliance is redirected toward murder, while the local Form II keeps causation of compliance as the selected force.
topics.reason: The broader ṭ-w-ʿ range is coherent, but the local Form II and object {{ar:قَتْلَ}} ({{tr:qatla}}) narrow it to making the act compliant rather than bare obedience.

topics.headline: Form II makes the self manufacture compliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wording does not say murder was simply easy; it says the self worked the barrier into compliance.
topics.reason: The Form II tag and causative/intensive grammar directly support this topic; the qiraat/intensification rows sharpen the same pressure.

topics.headline: qiraat variants expose pressure but do not control the parse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a variant-reading pressure toward reciprocity, while the canonical local surface remains Form II causation.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as apparatus, but the aligned local form is {{ar:طَوَّعَتْ}} ({{tr:ṭawwaʿat}}), so it cannot govern the canonical parse.

topics.headline: compliance feeds the killing and the loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that compliance vocabulary is not neutral here; it is the first motor in the ayah's route to violence and loss.
topics.reason: The local sequence explicitly places {{ar:طَوَّعَتْ}} ({{tr:ṭawwaʿat}}) before both q-t-l forms and the loss closure.

topics.headline: 3:168 inversely gathers obedience, brothers, and killing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 3:168 reverses similar ingredients, making 5:30 an internal-compliance version of the obedience-brother-killing field.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete reference (3:168), and nothing in the local grammar blocks it as an echo.

topics.headline: form, variants, and boundary make responsibility visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the convergence: morphology, variant pressure, and prior warning all make the killing textually owned rather than forced.
topics.reason: This row synthesizes already-licensed local evidence rather than adding a separate unsupported claim.

words.gloss_range: lām plus 3ms suffix: directed recipient or affected possessor, framed as false benefit
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahū}}) directs the self's work toward the killer as the affected recipient: murder is made compliant for him. That beneficiary-like grammar becomes bitterly ironic once the ayah ends with {{ar:ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-khāsirīna}}); the supposed service is self-harm. The repeated 3ms suffix also carries him through beneficiary, possessor of the self, possessor of the brother, and object roles.

topics.headline: lām directs the prompting toward him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the self's work is aimed at the killer as affected recipient before the self and murder are named.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the lām phrase as the prepositional complement of {{ar:طَوَّعَتْ}} ({{tr:ṭawwaʿat}}).

topics.headline: benefit grammar turns into self-harm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that what is grammatically made for him becomes the route by which he joins the losers.
topics.reason: The local outcome {{ar:ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-khāsirīna}}) supports the false-benefit reading of the lām role.

topics.headline: same suffix loops through possessor roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated 3ms suffix carrying the killer through beneficiary, self, brother, and victim roles.
topics.reason: The repeated suffixes are visible in the aligned word forms and preserve a concrete local relation.

words.gloss_range: possessed abstract noun as nominative subject: his own self becomes the internal agent
words.root_gloss_range: self, person, appetite, psyche, breath, and life-force; locally the possessed self acts as subject and internal cause
words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسُهُۥ}} ({{tr:nafsuhū}}) resolves the feminine verb and names his own possessed self as the subject of the prompting. The life/self range sharpens the paradox: the life-bearing inner self becomes the motor of life-taking, then disappears when the body executes the act in {{ar:قَتَلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:qatalahū}}). The self and brother share possessive framing, so the closing loss reads as the actor's own relational collapse. The same n-f-s and q-t-l field will be generalized in the killing-a-self rule (5:32).

topics.headline: nominative possessed self is the subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the killer's own possessed self is made the grammatical agent of the prompting.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative subject of {{ar:طَوَّعَتْ}} ({{tr:ṭawwaʿat}}), and its suffix makes the self particular to the killer.

topics.headline: life-bearing self enables life-taking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paradox that the life/self field becomes the inner motor of killing, while local grammar keeps this as agency of his self rather than a claim that every n-f-s branch is active.
topics.reason: The broad n-f-s range is relevant as pressure, but the local selected sense is the possessed self as subject.

topics.headline: n-f-s and q-t-l point toward 5:32
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the narrative self-and-killing field becomes the legal killing-a-self formulation in 5:32.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete nearby references (5:32), and the local ayah contains both n-f-s and q-t-l.

topics.headline: self initiates, body executes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural pivot from named inner agency to compressed outward action.
topics.reason: The first clause names {{ar:نَفْسُهُۥ}} ({{tr:nafsuhū}}) as subject, while the second verb carries only implicit subject agreement.

topics.headline: self, brother, and loss form a relational collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that his self and his brother share possessive framing, and the closing loss turns that internal action back on the actor.
topics.reason: The local suffix chain and closing loss word support the self-to-loss bookend; 5:25 is retained only as a concrete contrast where cited.

words.gloss_range: accusative maṣdar object: the abstract act of killing, specified by the brother in construct
words.root_gloss_range: killing, decisive termination, subduing, and mastery; locally narrowed to the abstract concept of physical killing as object of prompting
words.prose: {{ar:قَتْلَ}} ({{tr:qatla}}) is not yet the deed but the maṣdar object made compliant by the self. In construct with {{ar:أَخِيهِ}} ({{tr:akhīhi}}), the abstract act is already specified as the killing of his brother; the wider q-t-l range is narrowed here to physical murder, with decisive finality and kinship charge. It then echoes as the completed verb {{ar:قَتَلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:qatalahū}}), and the particular murder is positioned for the generalized killing-a-self rule (5:32).

topics.headline: maṣdar object names the act before execution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that murder first appears as an abstract object the self can work on before it appears as an event.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:قَتْلَ}} ({{tr:qatla}}) as an accusative maṣdar object of {{ar:طَوَّعَتْ}} ({{tr:ṭawwaʿat}}).

topics.headline: construct binds killing to the brother as patient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the abstract killing is already specified as his brother's killing, not a generic violent idea.
topics.reason: The iḍāfa attachment makes {{ar:أَخِيهِ}} ({{tr:akhīhi}}) the genitive complement, and the later object suffix confirms the objective reading.

topics.headline: q-t-l range narrows to physical murder
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the decisive q-t-l finality and kinship charge, while the human brother object narrows the sense to physical life-taking rather than mastery or dilution.
topics.reason: The broader q-t-l range survives as pressure, but the local complement {{ar:أَخِيهِ}} ({{tr:akhīhi}}) and later {{ar:قَتَلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:qatalahū}}) select concrete murder.

topics.headline: particular q-t-l anticipates 5:32 law
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this particular killing is positioned to become the generalized q-t-l and n-f-s rule in 5:32.
topics.reason: The concrete reference 5:32 is supplied by the CRITICAL rows and shares the q-t-l/n-f-s field.

topics.headline: q-t-l moves from concept to completed deed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same root move from processable concept to abrupt executed verb.
topics.reason: The local repetition of q-t-l in different forms directly supports the thought-to-deed movement.

words.gloss_range: genitive five-noun kinship term: his brother as the specified patient of the killing concept
words.root_gloss_range: brotherhood, kinship, companionship, and shared identity; locally the possessed brother is the patient of the killing concept
words.prose: {{ar:أَخِيهِ}} ({{tr:akhīhi}}) makes the victim visible first as kin, not merely as an object pronoun. Its genitive five-noun form is governed by {{ar:قَتْلَ}} ({{tr:qatla}}), while the possessive suffix binds the victim to the killer; the later object suffix compresses that brother into the completed act. The wider brotherhood field keeps shared-origin pressure active, and 2:178 shows kinship language persisting even inside murder law. The possessive echo with the self makes the act collapse the killer's own relational world, before 5:31 carries the brotherhood scene into aftermath.

topics.headline: genitive brother completes the killing construct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the victim is grammatically defined through kinship and governed by the killing concept.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:أَخِيهِ}} ({{tr:akhīhi}}) the genitive complement of {{ar:قَتْلَ}} ({{tr:qatla}}).

topics.headline: brotherhood carries shared-origin pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object is not anonymous but one bound by shared origin, while the local possessive keeps biological brotherhood primary.
topics.reason: The wider akh range is relevant, but the local narrative and possessive suffix narrow it to his brother.

topics.headline: brotherhood persists through murder law
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that kinship language remains active even inside murder and retaliation fields, including 2:178.
topics.reason: The row supplies the concrete reference (2:178), and it coheres with the local brother-killing frame.

topics.headline: victim appears as kin before object pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structure moving from named kinship to compressed objecthood and then onward to the aftermath in 5:31.
topics.reason: The local phrase names the brother before the later object suffix; the 5:31 forward echo is concrete and compatible.

topics.headline: his self and his brother mirror each other
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that matching possessive sounds make the killing feel like collapse inside the killer's own relational world.
topics.reason: The possessive chain is visible locally, and the same aftermath formula continues in 5:31.

words.gloss_range: second fa-link marking the killing as immediate consequence of the internal compliance clause
words.prose: The second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the killing the immediate result of the inner compliance clause. It is the middle hinge of the ayah's chain, moving psychology into action without inserting a new deliberative pause.

topics.headline: second fa makes killing the result of prompting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no independent deliberation is inserted between inner compliance and killing.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the killing clause to the prompting clause by sequence, and the CRITICAL rows preserve causal force.

topics.headline: middle fa moves psychology into action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second connector as the middle pulse in the ayah's three-beat chain.
topics.reason: The three fa particles visibly structure the ayah as inner process, outward act, and resulting state.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect active verb with object suffix: the abstract killing has become completed fratricide
words.root_gloss_range: killing, decisive termination, subduing, and mastery; locally Form I perfect active killing with explicit object suffix
words.prose: {{ar:قَتَلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:qatalahū}}) turns the earlier concept into completed fact. The active perfect keeps the killer recoverable in the verb's agreement while fusing the victim into the attached object suffix, so the single word is both compressed deed and new cause of loss. It stands between the self that prompted the act and the loss that follows, with 5:32 later turning killing into a legal generalization.

topics.headline: perfect active verb lands the irreversible act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deed is completed and active, not passive or deagentivized.
topics.reason: The verb is Form I perfect active with recoverable 3ms subject and explicit object suffix.

topics.headline: suffix morphology splits killer and victim roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the killer is carried by agreement while the victim is fused into the verb as object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the object suffix, while finite agreement carries the subject.

topics.headline: Form I with human object selects direct killing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices agency return from the self to the human actor as the broader q-t-l range narrows to direct fratricide.
topics.reason: The human object and active Form I verb block figurative q-t-l branches for the local selected sense.

topics.headline: q-t-l bridges the self field to the loss field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the completed killing standing between the self that prompted it and the loss that follows, with 5:32 as a later legal generalization.
topics.reason: The local order and the concrete 5:32 reference support this bridge without inventing a new topic.

topics.headline: single-word killing compresses the deed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the long internal setup collapses into one compact word that then becomes the cause of loss.
topics.reason: The verb is framed by fa-particles and repeats the earlier q-t-l maṣdar, so compression and root echo are local.

words.gloss_range: third fa-link marking loss as immediate consequence of the completed killing
words.prose: The third {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the state of loss the consequence of the killing. It closes the causal cadence begun at the opening particle: inner compliance, outward act, resultant classification.

topics.headline: third fa makes loss the result of killing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that loss is not an afterthought; it is grammatically caused by the killing.
topics.reason: The third fa links the killing clause to the resulting state clause in the attachment evidence.

topics.headline: final fa completes the causal cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the third connector close the chain from psychology to act to state.
topics.reason: The repeated particles at words 1, 7, and 9 are visible and locally structure the ayah.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect state-entry verb: he entered a classified state of loss, with dawn-manifestation pressure
words.root_gloss_range: morning, first light, manifestation, and entering a state; locally Form IV state-entry governs the loss predicate while retaining dawn-exposure color
words.prose: {{ar:أَصْبَحَ}} ({{tr:aṣbaḥa}}) shifts from event narration to state-entry. As a kāna-sister verb it governs {{ar:مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-khāsirīna}}) as predicate, while the ṣ-b-ḥ morning field makes the consequence feel exposed and manifest. The opening compliance verb and this closing state-entry verb both mark transformation, and 5:31 repeats the aftermath movement with regret.

topics.headline: aṣbaḥa enters a loss predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the killer enters a new classified condition rather than merely receiving a static label.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks a kāna-type clause with {{ar:مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-khāsirīna}}) as predicate complement.

topics.headline: morning light makes consequence visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices dawn and manifestation coloring the state change, while the local predicate keeps becoming one of the losers as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The ṣ-b-ḥ morning field survives as image, but the local grammar selects state-entry into a predicate rather than a bare time report.

topics.headline: fa-aṣbaḥa opens an aftermath formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:30's loss is the first aftermath state and 5:31 deepens the formula with regret.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete same-surah references (5:31 and 5:53), and the local phrase matches the aftermath frame.

topics.headline: opening and closing verbs both transform
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah bracketed by transformations: the self makes murder compliant, and the killer becomes one of the losers.
topics.reason: The semantic echo is local and non-root-based, supported by the two transformation verbs and the prior prediction boundary.

words.gloss_range: partitive preposition completing the predicate frame: he is placed among a pre-existing loss category
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) supplies the partitive classification frame. The killer does not become loss itself; he is placed among an established class, and the preposition keeps {{ar:ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-khāsirīna}}) tightly attached to the same state-entry predicate. The same category grammar carries the warning boundary (5:29) into loss here and onward toward regret (5:31).

topics.headline: min completes category membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that he does not become abstract loss; he is placed among an already recognizable category of losers.
topics.reason: QAC marks the preposition as partitive and attachment evidence makes it the predicate complement frame.

topics.headline: min carries the closing category chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same category grammar carrying the warning into loss and onward toward the next aftermath category.
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete adjacent references (5:29 and 5:31), and the local min-phrase supports category membership.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural active participle: an established class of those characterized by loss
words.root_gloss_range: deficiency, capital loss, failure, ruin, and perdition; locally an active-participle plural class of continuing loss
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-khāsirīna}}) is the ayah's closure landing: a definite plural active participle that classifies the actor among those characterized by ongoing loss. The kh-s-r field lets the ending read as catastrophic depletion: the self that initiated the act, the brother who was killed, and the killer's moral capital all collapse into loss. That individual loss participates in a Surah 5 aftermath formula that later scales to collective loss (5:53), while the self-to-loss ring makes the actor's own agency return as identity.

topics.headline: definite plural marks an established loser class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the killer is classified among a known group, not merely described by a private adjective.
topics.reason: The definite plural active participle is governed by {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) as the closing predicate complement.

topics.headline: active participle makes loss an ongoing status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing word assigns an enduring moral and existential state after the killing.
topics.reason: The active participle form and predicate position support ongoing classification rather than a one-time report only.

topics.headline: commercial loss image gathers self and brother
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the failed-transaction image: the killer spends self, brother, and standing for no gain, while local grammar keeps loss as the selected outcome category.
topics.reason: The kh-s-r range includes capital loss and ruin; the local self and brother terms make that image meaningful without replacing the predicate sense.

topics.headline: individual loss anticipates communal loss in 5:53
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 5:30's individual loss entering a surah-local formula that later applies to collective aftermath in 5:53.
topics.reason: The concrete references (5:53 and the wider loss register) are supplied by CRITICAL rows and cohere with the local formula.

topics.headline: closing loss returns to the opening self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's ring: the possessed self initiates the murder, and loss closes back over the actor as identity.
topics.reason: The self/loss bookend is visible locally, with the next ayah's regret ending (5:31) as a concrete forward echo.

baseline_models.mechanism: The self is cast as an inner agent that smooths and encourages a resisted possibility until fratricide becomes doable; the move from the nominal killing to the finite he-killed-him marks conversion of inward facilitation into completed act.

activation_trace.role: Supplies the literal easing and encouragement by the self, functioning as the mechanism that lowers resistance to the act.
Locates intention and deliberative content within the self, allowing it to operate as an internal persuader.
The repeated life-ending sense links the contemplated object directly to its execution.
Makes the target a kin relation rather than an interchangeable victim, intensifying what the self must make easy.

changed_reading.before: A man simply decided to kill his brother.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an internal production process: the self first makes fratricide compliant and feasible, and only then does the contemplated killing become an accomplished verb.

baseline_models.mechanism: A living self and a brotherly tether are joined in the victim; killing severs that tether and removes life, so the killer's loss is reflexive diminution of his own relational self rather than an external penalty alone.

activation_trace.role: Contributes life-bearing selfhood, making murder removal of a living person rather than only an aggressive motion.
Images brotherhood as a fastening bond, so killing functions as severance of a relation that also held the killer.
Supplies the irreversible removal that breaks the living bond.
Frames the result as subtraction from the killer, not acquisition through eliminating a rival.

changed_reading.before: He loses something as a consequence of killing another person.
changed_reading.after: By extinguishing his brother's life and cutting their tether, he diminishes the relational structure of his own self; the homicide is already self-loss.

baseline_models.mechanism: The completed act immediately changes the actor's standing. The commercial branch of loss casts the apparent success of killing as a transaction that consumes its own capital and enrolls him among deficit-bearers.

activation_trace.role: Provides the completed act that triggers the following change of state.
Marks becoming rather than merely feeling, assigning a new condition after the deed.
Contributes the failed-trade image, making the supposedly advantageous murder a destruction of capital.

changed_reading.before: The killer later suffers an unspecified bad consequence.
changed_reading.after: The murder itself closes as a losing exchange: accomplishment and deficit coincide, and the actor immediately becomes a member of the losing class.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding dialogue first voices a future killing, then explicitly opens and refuses a hand-for-hand killing relation. Against that refusal, the focus self's facilitation is no longer generic temptation: it is what carries a threat across the victim's nonreciprocity into unilateral execution.

activation_trace.role: Functions as the inner encouragement that overcomes the absence of reciprocal aggression.
Registers the threat's eventual realization as actual life-taking.
Supplies the announced but not yet executed killing, establishing the unrealized starting point.
Makes extension of the hand the practical interface of violence and marks the victim's refusal to activate that interface.
Opens a possible two-party combat frame only for the victim's speech to decline his side of it.

structural_cues: 5:27 places killing in a quoted future threat; 5:30 repeats it first as a nominal object and then as a completed finite verb.
5:28 mirrors hand extension and killing across two speakers but negates the victim's corresponding action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies threat, mirrored hand language, refusal, and later execution; I infer that self-facilitation bridges the blocked reciprocal frame into one-sided violence. Alternatively, the dialogue may only narrate escalation without specifying what inward resistance was overcome.

changed_reading.before: The self makes a violent intention easy.
changed_reading.after: The self manufactures unilateral executability precisely where the other brother has refused to make the encounter mutual.

context_deltas.mechanism: The self can facilitate the difficult destructive act, but after the killing the actor cannot devise the elementary care of covering his brother until shown. This ability inversion recasts self-facilitation as selective competence: agency is efficient toward destruction and deficient toward custodial aftermath.

activation_trace.role: Contributes attained capacity, which the aftermath exposes as narrowly available for the killing.
Identifies the self as what made the destructive task easy, setting up the later competence reversal.
Keeps both violence and failed care attached to the same brotherly relation.
Supplies the concrete custodial task of placing the exposed body out of sight.
Names the actor's incapacity after his self had already produced capacity for murder.
Makes belated regret arise from confronting the failed aftermath rather than from preventing the act.

structural_cues: The same brother recurs as the object first of killing and then of covering.
Demonstration by a nonhuman agent intervenes between the actor's incapacity and his regret.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies facilitation, completed killing, inability, demonstrated covering, and regret; I infer a morally inverted distribution of competence. A live alternative is simple ignorance of burial practice rather than a diagnosis of selective agency.

changed_reading.before: His self grants him enough resolve to perform the murder.
changed_reading.after: His agency is distorted rather than simply strong: it can make fratricide easy but cannot generate care for the brotherly body it has produced.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent repetition of became-among with different complements separates two stages. Killing first makes him one of the losers; only after the body's exposure and the lesson in covering does he become one of the regretful. Loss therefore cannot be reduced to remorse.

activation_trace.role: Marks the first acquired state immediately after killing.
Names objective diminution as the first post-deed classification.
Repeats the same state-transition operator after a further episode, making a second stage visible.
Supplies retrospective sorrow as the later state, distinct from the prior loss.

structural_cues: 5:30 and 5:31 close with the same فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ construction.
The covering episode stands between membership among the losers and membership among the regretful.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact syntactic echo with ordered, different predicates; I infer that the order differentiates objective loss from conscious regret. Alternatively, the two labels can overlap affectively even while the narration stages them separately.

changed_reading.before: Calling him a loser means that he regretted the murder.
changed_reading.after: The act constitutes loss before the narrative displays regret; remorse is a later recognition of a deficit already incurred.

context_deltas.mechanism: The explicit causal bridge carries this killing into an obligatory formulation, and the paired killing-preserving comparison scales one life to humanity as an undiminished whole. The murdered brother becomes a representative human relation; the killer's loss expands from private damage to subtraction from the shared human total.

activation_trace.role: Provides the severed brotherly tether that can be generalized as a human bond.
Supplies diminution, now enlarged from one actor's deficit to damage to a collective whole.
Makes the preceding event an explicit cause for the following normative expansion.
Converts the event's implication into an established, obligating judgment.
Repeats life-taking on both the individual and humanity-wide sides of the comparison.
Identifies the protected unit as living selfhood and supports equivalence between lives.
Supplies humanity in contrast to the nonhuman, widening the brother from kin member to human representative.
Contributes completeness without missing parts, so one killing registers as damage to the human whole.
Provides the counter-mechanism of preserving life by refraining from killing, clarifying what the focus act destroys.

structural_cues: 5:32 begins with an explicit because-of-that bridge from the preceding episode.
Killing one life and preserving one life are each compared with all humanity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the causal bridge, legal inscription, and individual-to-total comparison; I infer that the focus loss includes communal subtraction and that brotherhood is the local instance of human solidarity. Alternatively, 5:32 may generalize the rule without defining the semantic range of الخاسرين.

changed_reading.before: Fratricide destroys one kin relationship and makes its perpetrator lose.
changed_reading.after: The brother's death is the local fracture through which loss becomes species-wide: removing one life damages the imagined completeness of humanity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later written life-for-life sequence supplies measured public equivalence and even a route of voluntary relinquishment. Set against it, the focus self privately authorizes an irreversible taking. The deficient-measure branch of loss makes fratricide an act that shortchanges the brother's life by replacing accountable measure with inward permission.

activation_trace.role: Functions as private facilitation, the unauthorized inner substitute for a measured public process.
Contributes short measure, rendering the killing a radical undervaluation of the brother's life.
Supplies an established obligation against which private self-authorization can be contrasted.
Places living self against living self as the unit that must be measured rather than casually removed.
Contributes calibrated matching of consequence to injury, the opposite of unilateral fratricide.
Adds voluntary surrender of a due claim, distinguishing accountable generosity from the focus self's destructive easing.

structural_cues: 5:45 arranges life and body parts in repeated balanced pairs.
The measured sequence allows the holder of a claim to relinquish it, unlike the victim's unchosen loss in 5:30.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies self-facilitation, a loss branch of deficient measure, and later calibrated reciprocity; I infer that private murder is an under-measuring of life and a usurpation of judgment. Alternatively, the later rule can regulate a different legal setting without retrospectively specifying the focus loss.

changed_reading.before: خاسرين evokes a broadly losing outcome after murder.
changed_reading.after: The killer is a loser also as a false measurer: his self treats a brother's life as expendable where accountable equivalence treats life as irreducible.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later two-ayah chain moves from what is hidden in selves, through becoming regretful, to intended deeds collapsing and the exact formula becoming losers. That echo exposes the focus architecture: inwardly managed purpose becomes outward act, but the apparent achievement nullifies itself and fixes a public state of loss.

activation_trace.role: Locates the enabling purpose inside the actor before it externalizes as killing.
Converts the private-to-active sequence into an acquired, visible status.
Names the resulting deficit that the later echo ties to collapsed action.
Supplies concealment in the interior, sharpening the focus self as a hidden site of operative purpose.
Repeats the self as container of intent, linking inward calculation to later exposure.
Adds belated sorrow when the concealed calculation meets its outcome.
Contributes collapse and descent, making the actors' purposeful deeds lose effective value.
Identifies what collapses as intentional action, paralleling the focus movement from intent to deed.
Repeats the focus transition into an assigned condition.
Completes the exact later echo by naming diminution after deeds have failed.

structural_cues: 5:52 places concealed content in selves immediately before regret.
5:53 couples collapsed deeds with the same أصبحوا خاسرين closure used in singular form at 5:30.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the inner-self sequence, regret, deed-collapse, and exact loss formula; I infer a shared causal architecture in which a privately pursued gain self-nullifies. Alternatively, the later actors form an independent analogy and the repeated closure may be thematic rather than mechanistically identical.

changed_reading.before: The self successfully produces a murder and loss is an added consequence.
changed_reading.after: The inward project externalizes successfully only at the surface; at the level of value, the deed collapses into the very loss-status it produces.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later branch image of making something pliant after difficulty occurs in a relational instruction that places yielding on the side of fellow believers. It reorients the focus easing as a misallocated capacity: inward pliancy is used to overcome inhibition against harming a brother rather than to sustain gentleness toward him.

activation_trace.role: Supplies the focus's making-easy process, whose object is the brother's killing.
Anchors the moral misdirection in a relation that ordinarily calls for solidarity.
Provides a second making-pliant image in a pro-social relation, exposing the focus facilitation as directed toward the wrong end.

5:30 directs an easing process toward killing the explicitly named brother.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two facilitation or pliancy images and contrasting relational objects; I infer moral misallocation of a neutral capacity. changed_reading.before: The self's easing is simply an increase in violent resolve.
changed_reading.after: The tragedy includes a reversal of relational pliancy: the faculty that could soften conduct toward a brother instead softens the prohibition against destroying him.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the brother's wasted blood makes the project void at inception: the apparent gain is a deed that cancels its own value and leaves only loss.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it couples a nonprimary dawn-opening branch of نفس with the literal-morning branch of أصبح and later concealment imagery. It remains anchored in adjacent focus roots and the packet's repeated hiding-and-becoming pattern; render it only as an evoked exposure image, never as a replacement translation for نفسه or أصبح.

activation_trace.role: Contributes an opening or spreading like daybreak, imaging the inward impulse as something that will emerge.

changed_reading.before: He simply becomes a loser after the act.
changed_reading.after: As a contained poetic activation, what the self prepared inwardly breaks open like dawn: the corpse may be covered, but the killer's loss has passed into exposure.

strongest_changes: The victim's refusal of reciprocal violence makes the self's facilitation specifically a bridge to unilateral execution.
The exact adjacent أصبح construction shows that loss is incurred before regret is narrated.
The causal and humanity-wide comparison in 5:32 scales severed brotherhood into damage to the human whole.
The later echo of hidden selves, collapsed deeds, and becoming losers reveals the murder as an inward project that nullifies its own gain.
summary.what_was_special: This focus is unusually activated by reversals of capacity and scale: the self can enable killing but not care, one brother can stand for humanity's completeness, and an apparently successful deed can itself constitute deficit. Exact later repetitions of نفس, أصبح, and خسر keep these mechanisms anchored while allowing the wasted-blood and dawn-exposure branches to remain visible as contained outliers.
remaining_uncertainties: The extent to which الخاسرين in the focus itself carries commercial or deficient-measure imagery rather than general diminution remains open.
The legal reciprocity of 5:45 may illuminate the focus retrospectively without defining the original killer's precise loss.
The pliancy, wasted-blood, and dawn-exposure readings depend on branch-level analogy and should coexist with, not displace, the direct internal-facilitation reading.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The self manufactures ease for the forbidden act.** `ط و ع B006` is making an act easy to oneself, `ن ف س B013` hidden intent, and `ق ت ل B002` subduing until force is softened. I infer that inner rehearsal softens resistance before the external killing occurs. “His self made it compliant” reads as a process of moral friction-removal.
2. **Morning exposes the loss.** `ص ب ح B001` is the opening of dawn and `خ س ر B001` deficiency. The result becomes visible at morning-like disclosure: apparent mastery is revealed as subtraction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The self makes murder pliant before the hand performs it.** Fixed **ط و ع / B001** (“pliant obedience and willing yielding”) and **B006** (“making an act easy to oneself”) assign the enabling role to the killer’s *nafs*. The sequence places inner facilitation before killing and immediate loss after it; 5:31 then exposes his incapacity before a simple burial task. I infer that desire rehearses away resistance until the act feels executable. The ayah therefore reads as an account of internal moral engineering, not an unexplained leap from anger to homicide.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:31 was the sharp correction: the self that made killing easy immediately confronted inability before the simpler task of covering its result.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesindeki kullanımlar, belirli öznelerin yarılması, açılması, uzayıp genişlemesi veya suyu artarak yayılması ortak görüntüsünde birleşir. Bu anlam yalnızca verilen kalıplarda geçerlidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca yay, sabah, gündüz ve ırmakla kurulan kalıplara bağlıdır; çıplak kök anlamına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Yalnızca belirli kalıplarda, yayın yarılması; sabahın açılması; gündüzün uzayıp genişlemesi veya ırmak suyunun artıp yayılmasıdır. Ortak görüntü, kapalı ya da dar bir durumdan açılma ve genişlemeye geçiştir.

facets.statement: Yay için kullanıldığında yarılma ya da çatlama olayını bildirir.
Sabah ve gündüz için kullanıldığında aydınlığın açılmasını, sürenin uzayıp genişlemesini bildirir.
Irmak ya da dalga için kullanıldığında suyun artıp dışarı doğru yayılmasını bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak kaydı, yaydaki çatlama, sabahtaki açılma, gündüzdeki genişleme ve sudaki artışı kalıba bağlı bir açılma-yayılma görüntüsünde birleştirir.

concept_gloss.text: kalıba bağlı yarılıp açılma ve genişleme

contextual_glosses.applicability: Irmak suyunun yükselip çevreye doğru yayılması kalıbında kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bedeni canlı tutan ilkeyi, onun bedenden çıkmasıyla ölümü ve her insanın canlı bir birey olarak bu adla sayılabilmesini doğrudan açıklar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak dal, bedene yaşam veren canı ve bununla canlı sayılan bireyi kapsar; kalıp anlamı içe aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bedeni canlı tutan ve ayrılmasıyla ölümün gerçekleştiği candır. Bu yaşam taşıyıcısı bakımından her insan ayrı bir canlı birey olarak da sayılabilir.

facets.statement: Bedene yaşam veren ve bedenden ayrılması ölüm sayılan candır.
Bu canı taşıyan her insan ayrı bir canlı birey olarak adlandırılabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bedensel yaşamı sağlayan can, bu canın çıkmasıyla ölüm ve insanın canlı birey olarak sayılması üzerinde birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Canlılığı sağlayan ve bedenden ayrılması ölüm anlamına gelen yaşam taşıyıcısı için uygundur.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى عين الشيء، ذاته، حقيقته، جملته، كنهه وجوهره، واستعمالها للتوكيد.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, canın bedenden ayrılmasına yol açan öldürme eylemini ve bu sonucu doğuran çeşitli araçları açıkça bildirir. İnsan bedeninde vurulduğunda ölüm getiren yerler de aynı çekirdeğe bağlı özel bir kullanımdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım temel öldürme anlamını verir; kötü biçimde öldürme ve bedendeki ölümcül noktalar yalnızca kendi kalıplarına bağlı tutulur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi boyun eğdirme ve işe alıştırma çekirdeğini destekler; deneyimli kişi kullanımı ise şiddetin yumuşaması değil, işlerce sınanıp pişmiş olma sonucudur. Bu nedenle çerçeve, eğitim ile deneyim sonucunu ayırarak kullanılabilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel edilgenleştirme ve alıştırma anlamı, hayvanın işe alışmışlığı ile insanın deneyim kazanmışlığını bildiren kalıplardan ayrı gösterilir.

facets.statement: Bir insanı ya da hayvanı direnci kırılmış ve uysal duruma getirme ya da özellikle hayvanı bir işe alıştırmadır.
